title: Mother-Plant Identity and Health Status
objective: Build a mother-stock identity and health system that separates provenance, visible condition, laboratory status, and propagation performance.

terms.definition: A maintained donor plant from which cuttings or explants are repeatedly collected for propagation.
A plant that supplies tissue used to create vegetative propagules or explants.
The documented origin, identity history, and custody of plant material.
Plant material that has passed a defined identity and health-release program for a stated test scope.
Controlled isolation of incoming or uncertain material while identity and health status are evaluated.
An infection that is present without obvious visible symptoms at the time of observation.
The documented decision to allow, restrict, reject, or continue holding material based on defined criteria.

coreScience: A mother plant is both a genetic source and a biological reservoir. Every cutting inherits tissue from that donor, so mother identity, health, nutrition, stress history, and infection status affect the entire downstream clone batch.

Visual inspection can identify obvious pests, lesions, distortion, nutrient stress, and poor vigor, but it cannot prove absence of latent viruses, viroids, endophytes, or systemic pathogens. Hop latent viroid is especially important because infected plants may be propagated before severe symptoms appear, allowing the clone network to distribute the agent.

Clean stock should mean material that has passed a defined identity and health-release program. It should not mean merely ‘looks clean.’ A defensible program defines the organisms tested, sample tissue, method, laboratory, date, lot, retest interval, quarantine status, and release authority.
cultivationRelevance: Separate mother-stock areas from incoming clones and production rooms. Do not harvest cuttings from plants with unresolved identity, pest, disease, chemical-injury, or root-health findings. Retain a documented backup rather than relying on one irreplaceable donor.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Mother ID and provenance; acquisition and quarantine dates; genotype/chemotype records; pest and disease observations; laboratory sample IDs and results; nutrition and environment; cutting count; rooting and rejection rates; release and retirement decisions.

misconceptions: Mother plants only need to be vigorous.
No symptoms means no systemic pathogen.
One negative test permanently certifies a plant.
evidenceLimits: Testing sensitivity, tissue distribution, infection timing, and sampling method affect results. This lesson does not define a universal pathogen panel or legal release standard.
